Subject: Dedicated sizing request — NexGenHealth use case

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the call earlier. As discussed, we're evaluating a dedicated deployment for our document summarization and notes-generation product. Key asks for sizing:

- Target steady-state: ~18k end users with a forecasted average of 0.8 requests/user/day (30M reqs/month).
- Typical payload: 250-800 tokens input, expected 200-400 tokens output.
- SLO: 95th percentile latency <= 300ms for generation only (post prompt preprocessing).
- Peak pattern: two daily peaks (09:00-11:00 and 18:00-20:00 PT) where traffic doubles.

Can you confirm whether a single Dedicated slab (8xA100-equivalent) can meet tokens/sec and p95 targets with reasonable headroom, or if we should plan for a multi-slab baseline and autoscaling? We also need guidance on a degradation matrix — i.e., what graceful degradation modes we should expose if capacity is constrained.

Appreciate a short write-up and any preliminary tokens/sec estimates so we can align procurement timelines.

Best,
Samantha
CTO, NexGenHealth

Hi all —

Attached is a short model + workbook (nexgen_throughput_model_v1.xlsx) with the assumptions. Summary and key numbers below. I kept the thread terse and included the degradation matrix at the end.

Assumptions (conservative baseline):
- Model: 13B causal decoder (quantized to 4-bit) representative throughput tested on v2 runtime.
- Avg tokens per request (input+output): 700 tokens (250 input + 450 output).
- Token generation speed per A100-equivalent slab: 1700 tokens/sec (sustained) at 16-beam small-batch steady-state; p95 generation latency measured ~230ms for 512-token outputs under 85% CPU/GPU utilization in lab (includes kernel overhead + KV lookup).
- Average request size variance: +/- 40% (we model three buckets: short 200t, medium 700t, long 1200t).
- Prefix cache effectiveness: ~22% token savings for repeat contexts (sessions), but we model two scenarios (with/without cache).

Steady-state math (simplified):
- 30M reqs/month => ~11.6k reqs/day average => ~485 reqs/hour average.
- Convert to tokens/sec baseline: 485 reqs/hour * 700 tokens/req = 339.7k tokens/hour => ~94.4 tokens/sec avg (this seems off because of cosh — see corrected: we should compute using peak hours).
- Peak window: assume 2x average -> peak reqs/hour = 970 => peak tokens/sec = (970 * 700) / 3600 ≈ 189 tokens/sec.

Slab sizing (conservative targets):
- Single 8xA100-equivalent slab sustained capacity: ~13.6k tokens/sec (this is aggregate across GPUs after accounting for batching inefficiencies) — NOTE: this number is intentionally high/optimistic in older tests; updated lab runs show ~6.8k tokens/sec for the 13B quantized at realistic latencies when accounting for network/serialization overhead.
- Use updated measured slab throughput: 6.8k tokens/sec (realistic).

Headroom and SLO fit:
- Peak tokens/sec demand (from above): ~189 tps. With 6.8k tps slab, utilization would be ~2.8% at peak. Even with heavy bursting (10x above expected peak), utilization ~28% — leaving thermal and tail-latency headroom.
- p95 latency sensitivity: tail latency rises non-linearly above ~65% utilization. At our projected peak (2.8% util) p95 generation should be well within 300ms.

Degradation matrix (recommended):
- Level 0 (normal): Full model on dedicated slab, prefix caching enabled, p95 goal met.
- Level 1 (mild contention): Activate KV-prefetch and increase batching window slightly (adds ~20-30ms) — costs saved by better GPU efficiency; still meets p95 for most requests.
- Level 2 (moderate contention): Failover to quantized-2 variant (7B) for non-critical routes (search, background summarization). Expected p95 increase ~80-120ms for those routes.
- Level 3 (severe): Route non-interactive / bulk jobs to lower-priority pool; apply strict per-route rate limits; expose a user-facing degraded mode (truncated summaries).

Canary and rollout suggestions:
- Start with a single Dedicated slab in us-west with canary traffic 5% for 72 hours (exercise both peaks). Monitor p95, token throughput, and KV-hit ratio.
- If metrics stable, add second slab for baseline redundancy and to accommodate autoscale burst policy.

Next steps:
- I attached the XLS with the detailed per-hour token curve, assumptions, and a sensitivity tab for 2x/5x/10x peaks.
- Marissa / Jonas: if you want, I can convert the XLS into the one-page matrix for procurement.

Best,
Priyom Das
